sections.html:
Jefferson County sits in central Oregon high desert, and Madras is the county seat. The 2020 census counted 24,502 residents, up 12.8% from 2010. The county covers 1,791 square miles and was created on December 12, 1914, from part of Crook County.

Two large blocks of land limit what can be owned here. The Warm Springs reservation, held by the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs, takes up about 21% of county land, and the U.S. Forest Service manages about 24%. If your parcel is near either boundary, ask the Assessor to confirm the tax status of the land before you list.

Crooked River Ranch is the largest unincorporated community, a census-designated place of 4,912 people in southern Jefferson County, between the Deschutes and Crooked rivers near Lake Billy Chinook. It covers about 12,000 acres and is described as the largest homeowner association in Oregon.

A house there comes with HOA rules and dues. Ask the association for its documents early, so a buyer sees them at the start and not in the middle of escrow.

The county Finance Department bills and collects property tax for every taxing district in Jefferson County. The office is at 66 SE D Street, Suite E, Madras. The Assessor is a separate department, so value questions go there and payment questions go to Finance.

The county's tax collection pages carry the forms you are likely to need: a mailing address change form, the tax statement guide, foreclosure information and an appeal guide titled How to Appeal Your Property Value.

Oregon's tax year runs July 1 to June 30. Statements go out by October 25, and the three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. When a date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

Oregon law, ORS 311.505, sets the discounts. Pay everything by the November due date and you take 3% off. Pay two-thirds and you take 2% off. Pay less than two-thirds and there is no discount.

Overdue taxes carry 1.33% interest a month, which is 16% a year. Interest posts on the 16th of each month until the account is paid.

If you plan to sell in the fall, decide who pays the November installment before you sign a purchase agreement. The title company will prorate it at closing, but only if the bill is current.

sections.h2: How to pay and what it costs
sections.html:
Mail, online and in-person payers follow slightly different timing rules.

  • By mail, a USPS postmark on or before the due date counts as on time under ORS 305.820. Make the check out to Jefferson County Tax.
  • With no postmark, the delivery date is used.
  • Online bill pay usually carries no postmark, so the money has to arrive by the due date.
  • Payments through Point and Pay count if sent by 11:59 pm on the 15th.
  • In person, the office takes cash, check, money order or card.

Card payments cost 2.50% (minimum $2.00). A Visa Signature debit card costs $3.95, and an eCheck costs $1.50. The county keeps none of these fees. To pay by card over the phone, call 1-877-865-0432.

Read the county's appeal guide first. If the value still looks wrong, file with the Property Value Appeals Board by December 31, after you receive your tax statement. A weekend or holiday deadline moves to the next business day. Call the Finance Department at 541-475-4458 to confirm the current filing date and where to deliver the petition.

If the board's order does not fix the problem, the Oregon Tax Court Magistrate Division hears value appeals filed within 30 days of the order. Exemption denials and special assessment disqualification have a 90 day window.

Oregon applies one foreclosure rule to every county. Real property can be foreclosed once three years have passed since the earliest delinquency date. The list is prepared in July and published in August. Paying the full tax and interest takes the property off the list, though a 5% penalty is added once the list is published.

After judgment, the redemption period is two years. The owner, an heir, a recorded lienholder or a city holding a lien may redeem by paying the taxes, interest, the penalty and a fee. If the house is worth more than the debt, the owner is entitled to the surplus.

A sale can still close with taxes owed. Here is the usual order:

  • Ask the Finance Department for a balance listed by year.
  • Give that balance to the buyer's title company.
  • Escrow pays the oldest years first and settles the rest from your proceeds at closing.

A cash buyer who closes without lender conditions can often move through this step faster, because there is no loan underwriting waiting on the payoff letter.

Farm acreage needs extra care. Land under Oregon's farm-use special assessment can owe additional tax for up to 10 years if it is disqualified, or five years inside an urban growth boundary. Ask the Assessor for the special assessment status of any acreage before you set a price.

Rural lots also raise questions a town lot does not. Hard freezes make pipe and well protection a real maintenance item, and sun and wide temperature swings wear on roofs and siding in this dry climate. Wildfire is a regional concern as well: the 2020 Santiam Fire burned in Jefferson County along with Marion, Linn and Clackamas.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Pull together four things before you ask for offers:

  • Your latest tax statement.
  • Well and septic records, if the lot is rural.
  • HOA documents, if the home is in Crooked River Ranch.
  • The special assessment status of any farm acreage.

Bring the statement and a photo ID when you visit the Finance office. Ask for a written balance, because a buyer's title company will want paper before it schedules closing.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Jefferson County, Oregon?
faqs.a: Madras. It was incorporated in 1911 and became the permanent seat after a 1916 election, replacing Culver as the temporary seat.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jefferson County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Finance Department, 66 SE D Street, Suite E, Madras, or by mail, phone (1-877-865-0432) or online through Point and Pay. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How much discount does Jefferson County give for early payment?
faqs.a: 3% for paying in full by the November due date and 2% for paying two-thirds. Paying less than two-thirds earns no discount.

faqs.q: What interest does Jefferson County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: 1.33% per month, or 16% a year, posting on the 16th of each month until paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jefferson County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount is settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a balance by year from the Finance Department so the title company can pay the oldest years first.
